components.claim: A conventional dense global-attention model provides the quality and systems anchor needed to interpret hybrid efficiency.
components.quality: All six frozen cells are complete. Candidate-minus-control endpoint loss is -0.039170/-0.042662/-0.037184 nats; mean -0.039672 and upper one-sided 95% bound -0.034996 pass the +0.01 margin. All eleven source bounds pass, so the whole-architecture proxy quality screen passes without component attribution.
components.systems: At 128K the historical dense geometry has about 1.92 GiB analytic BF16 state and 25.10 GFLOP/token. Across the proxy pairs, the candidate uses 21.49% fewer analytic FLOPs/token, 10.01% less steady time, 10.42% less active time, and 11.13% more steady throughput, but 20.77% more peak allocation. Mean time-to-quality improvement is 19.48% with lower one-sided 95% bound 16.83%; no pair is censored. Dense controls still fail the frozen 1.0-hour envelope, so no paired hard-envelope or serving claim passes.
unresolved_risks: six-pair finalist configs, data, storage, crossed-factor collector/analysis v2, and exact runtime qualify, but live launch remains blocked by HELMET transfer
RULER v1 failed its answer-anchored contamination gate; v2 excludes both QA tasks
HELMET still needs archive-external datasets, a gated truncation tokenizer, and model-judge qualification
one of 256000 native CUDA full-versus-cached logits misses the frozen parity tolerance, although all eight token argmaxes agree
components.next_gate: after HELMET acquisition exits, record one clean v2 live launch qualification before the first dense finalist control

components.claim: A recurrent/local backbone is cheaper than pervasive exact attention while preserving short-context language quality.
components.quality: GDN-global beats the convolution hybrid by 0.05002 nats; pure GDN loses 0.15499 nats relative to the attention-containing control.
components.systems: Qualified Torch and FLA training/prefill/decode paths on RTX 3090.
components.next_gate: retain as a matched control while finalists are tested at longer horizon

components.claim: Channel-wise decay plus NoPE improves long-range association while periodic global attention preserves exact lookup.
components.quality: The complete five-cache KDA/GQA architecture passes the three-pair whole-architecture proxy quality screen: mean paired endpoint loss -0.039672 nats, upper one-sided 95% bound -0.034996, and all eleven source bounds below their margins. This does not isolate or promote KDA, NoPE, GQA, or the 3:1 ratio.
components.systems: At the fixed endpoint the whole candidate averages 21.49% fewer analytic FLOPs/token, 10.01% less steady training time, and 11.13% higher throughput than dense, while peak allocation is 20.77% higher. Mean time-to-quality improves 19.48% with lower bound 16.83%. Exact-shape and cache-equivalence qualifications remain as previously recorded; no serving or paired hard-envelope claim follows.
components.runtime_support: Torch reference and isolated FLA kernels pass; powered trained-topology CUDA cache equivalence and exact-shape Paper 1 preflight v2 pass, while the hybrid production runtime remains incomplete
unresolved_risks: inference is limited to two fixed data orders; pooled six-cell df=5 output has no authority
whole-architecture result has no component attribution
RULER v1 failed its answer-anchored contamination gate; v2 excludes both QA tasks
HELMET's RAG/long-QA guardrail remains data, rights, tokenizer, and scorer blocked
components.next_gate: after HELMET acquisition exits, record one clean v2 live launch qualification before the first dense finalist control

components.claim: Three periodically refreshed global memories can replace five independent caches.
components.quality: Strict paired loss and candidate gates pass only two of three seeds; symbolic route retrieval is 0.53 versus 1.00 for five caches.
components.systems: Persistent state falls 1.66x and eager high-batch decode improves 1.31x, but compiled batch-one decode regresses and peak allocation does not fall.
components.scale_transfer: not attempted after proxy promotion failed
components.runtime_support: reference implementation and controlled PyTorch benchmarks
components.next_gate: no interaction or compression experiments on this topology without a new independent promotion result

components.claim: A learned attention output gate improves global attention quality enough to justify its cost.
components.quality: The 131M gain is 0.00234 nats, inside measured variance.
components.next_gate: none unless new independent evidence motivates a new policy version

components.claim: Compressing each of the five conservative global memories can reduce serving state without the Reader Attention capability loss.
components.systems: Conditional MQA1 and MLA128 each reduce five-cache BF16 state analytically by 66.7%; MQA1 parameter matching is within 0.00998%, while MLA128 is projection-parameter matched before implementation audit. No realized result exists.
components.next_gate: select the sequence backbone, then qualify MQA1 geometry and MLA128 reference/optimized correctness before any representation training

components.claim: Content-dependent depth routing improves quality per training FLOP in a deeper, narrower Speck model.
components.next_gate: after sequence selection, materialize the 40-module source graph and small-tensor standard/static/full/eight-block references

components.claim: Block-routed attention reduces long-context prefill cost while retaining retrieval and composition.
components.next_gate: select the parent/cache, then isolate the HCA compressor before rate; CSA begins only with oracle block-mass feasibility, followed by raw-local and integer ratio studies

components.claim: Conditional width improves quality per active training FLOP and serving dollar.

components.claim: Lower numerical precision reduces physical cost without changing model quality.
components.quality: INT8 KV capacity reference exists; production precision parity is not established.
